subject: POC plan: model choice, success metrics, and multilingual evaluation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@acmehealth.com>, Jared Connors <jared.connors@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, May 1, 2026 at 14:08 -0700
Subject: POC plan: model choice, success metrics, and multilingual evaluation

Hi Alice / Jared —

Thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Summary and proposed next steps below so we’re all aligned before we put the SOW together. I pulled this into a quick doc and attached a sample prompt set (see sample_prompts.csv) and a draft POC SOW (POC_SOW_draft.pdf).

High-level POC objective: Validate Redwood inference for Acme’s triage assistant across English + Spanish conversational traffic and ensure latency and cost meet your live requirements.

Proposed evaluation plan (3 weeks):
- Week 0: kickoff, access & infra (service account, test dataset, redwood dev keys)
- Week 1: model baseline & prompt tuning — run 500 representative prompts from your corpus (English/Spanish)
- Week 2: stress + latency testing with synthetic concurrency to match peak (up to 40 concurrent users)
- Week 3: qualitative review, fallback behavior test, and handoff report

Success criteria (provisional):
- Latency: p95 generation time <= 250ms for <512 token turns in hosted sandbox
- Accuracy / quality: primary metric = helpfulness score (human eval) >= 4.0 / 5 on a 100-sample cross-lingual test set
- Safety/regression: zero critical safety regressions vs. baseline on provided safety checklist
- Cost: projected per-1k-token inference cost <= 20% above your current baseline when using recommended quantization/profile

Model selection (recommended):
- Primary: Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized float16 path) — balances multilingual competence and latency on our Dedicated nodes
- Fallback: Mistral-Instruct-7B (fast, cheaper) — for low-latency degraded mode to keep SLAs in heavy load or regional failover
- Notes: we’ll run a quick head-to-head on a 100-pair English/Spanish prompt subset to verify Spanish fidelity. If Spanish falls short, we can test a specialized multilingual checkpoint (suggested reserve: M2M-100 proxy for translation evaluation).

Ownership and point people:
- Redwood (POC lead): Ben Carter — overall timeline, model tuning, infra config
- Redwood (security/compliance): Soojin Lee — data handling, logging, retention settings
- Acme (POC sponsor): Alice Ramos — evaluation signoffs, access to test sets

Next concrete steps by EOD Monday, May 4:
1) Acme: share the 500-sample test set + obfuscated PHI rules (Alice)
2) Redwood: confirm sandbox provisioned and share API keys + S3 ingestion instructions (Ben)
3) Both: quick 30-min kickoff calendar invite (Ben to schedule)

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Any hard constraints on on-prem only inference for legal/regulatory? You mentioned VPC preference but sounded open to hosted sandbox for the POC.
- Do you want transcripts stored for 30 days or shorter? This affects log retention and cost.

Thanks — I’ll push the working SOW after you confirm the timeline.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Connors <jared.connors@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, May 4, 2026 at 08:06 -0700
Subject: Re: POC plan: model choice, success metrics, and multilingual evaluation

Ben — thanks for the summary, looks sensible. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide the 500-sample set by Tuesday (May 5) but it will be de-identified — some utterances will lose context; hope that’s ok for a quality baseline.
- On-prem: for legal reasons Acme product teams prefer VPC-hosted or dedicated tenancy for any data containing PHI. Hosted sandbox is ok as long as data is pseudonymized and retention is short.
- Spanish coverage: we rely heavily on Latin American Spanish; if you can include accent/region variety in the test subset, that would be great.

Also, can you confirm what the fallback behavior looks like? If the primary model produces low-confidence answers, do we auto-fallback to Mistral-Instruct or do we surface a flag to users? We’d prefer a silent fallback for the assistant but want logs flagged for review.

Finally: budget guardrails — what’s a rough estimate for the 3-week POC (compute + engineering effort)? We need a ballpark to sign off.

—Alice
Director, Digital Products | Acme Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@acmehealth.com>, Jared Connors <jared.connors@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 4, 2026 at 09:14 -0700
Subject: Re: POC plan: model choice, success metrics, and multilingual evaluation

Thanks Alice — great questions. Short answers inline: 

- De-identified set: absolutely fine. We’ll note possible signal loss in the final report and run an augmented set if needed.
- VPC/Dedicated requirement: for the POC we can provision an isolated Dedicated sandbox in a VPC in your preferred cloud region. That meets the PHI constraint while keeping the POC automated. Soojin will confirm minimal controls required.
- Multilingual sampling: yes — please include Spanish samples tagged with locale (es-419, es-MX, es-ES) if possible. If not, include a note and we’ll expand the synthetic set.

Fallback behavior: default plan = silent auto-fallback to Mistral-Instruct-7B when model confidence score < threshold (we surface flagged logs to your audit S3 bucket). We can also configure a visible escalation path if you prefer (e.g., assistant responds with "I need to escalate to a human"). Recommend silent fallback for UX but flagged logs for QA.

POC ballpark (estimated):
- Redwood effort: 40 engineer hours (setup, tuning, analysis) — included in the standard POC package
- Cloud/compute: approximate hosted/dedicated runtime spend = $3k-$6k for the 3-week footprint depending on concurrency; fallback use reduces spend if invoked often
- Total budget: ~ $5k-$10k (we’ll firm up after model run profiling).

I’ll schedule the kickoff for Wed, May 6 at 10am PT unless you prefer another slot.

Ben

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 4, 2026 at 09:48 -0700
Subject: Re: POC plan: model choice, success metrics, and multilingual evaluation

Hi Alice — quick note from security/compliance:

- VPC/Dedicated sandbox is fine for the POC. We’ll set retention to 30 days by default and can shorten to 7 days if you need. Logs can be exported to your S3 bucket with AES-256 encryption and RBAC.
- We will not store raw transcripts containing PHI in plain text; Redwood will apply configured pseudonymization transforms before persisting.
- Please share any additional audit requirements (SOC 2 artifact requests, encryption key rotation windows) so we can list them in the SOW.

Soojin
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
